what: Hand a write buffer back on completion, so the store commits pack bytes with one copy fewer. Where: crates/blaze-core/src/lib.rs `Done`: add `WrittenAt(Vec<u8>)` as the completion of `Effect::WriteAt` (the bytes it was given, untouched, capacity kept), and give `Done::Failed` (or a new `FailedWrite { error, bytes }`) the same buffer for a failed `WriteAt`; every driver (uring, kqueue, iocp, sim) returns the Vec it wrote from. Why: blaze-cas commits a pack by copying pack memory into a fresh Vec for each WriteAt (crates/blaze-cas/src/lib.rs, the `Effect::WriteAt` push in the commit, `pack.memory[..].to_vec()`), because a failed write must be retried from the same bytes. That copy runs serially on the store thread at about 0.1 ns a byte plus page faults on the fresh Vec, against NVMe at 0.14 ns a byte: with the drain copy it puts a commit about 3x off the device bound (docs/v2/plan/lanes/store/speed-of-light.md, "Packs and the commit"). With the buffer handed back, blaze-cas moves the drained tail into the effect and takes it back on completion or failure; store (speed-sol2-store) makes that edit once this lands.
